requirement:
When authoring evidence for a requirement, its fenced declaration, including its complete body but excluding anchor option lines, MUST
be included in the mandatory input set defined by
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`.
rationale:
`requirements.authoring_input` has one obligation. When the subject is a requirement, its fenced declaration must be in the mandatory input set. That means the opening and closing fences and the complete body, but not the anchor option lines. The reviewed tests cover this as follows.

- `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[anchored_files_contribute_root_node_inputs]` is the main test.
  - The declaration has `:impl:` and `:test:` anchor lines, a multi-paragraph body with a blank line, and a body line that starts with `:impl: this is body text`.
  - It asserts that the first mandatory input equals an exact JSON object. Its `text` is `:::{req} ready`, the body lines including the blank line and the body-text `:impl:` line, and the closing `:::`.
  - The anchor option lines are absent from that text. This tests the exclusion, and also that only anchor option lines directly after the fence are dropped, not body lines that look like them.
  - The declaration input is `requirements.ready` itself, so the subject's own declaration is shown to be included.
  - The exact-equality check on the whole input list also rules out extra or missing contributions.
- `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[unresolvable_earlier_inputs_do_not_block_reassessment]` asserts exact equality of the mandatory inputs with a single declaration input. Its text is the full fenced text `:::{req} ready`, `The project MUST be ready.`, `:::`, and it carries the `requirements` and `matches` fields. This shows that the declaration is included even when earlier evidence is unusable.
- `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[bundle_combines_direct_references_terms_and_current_existing_selectors]` checks that the declaration input for `requirements.case` has the exact full text with fences. It also checks that the declaration appears alongside cited requirements and definitions, and that other inputs are deduplicated and combined.
- `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[mandatory_inputs_can_read_untracked_declarations_and_terms]` checks that declarations can be read when the book files are untracked in git. It also checks that the resulting inputs are produced.

All four tests are marked `{test}` for the subject. The assertions are exact, so an implementation that truncated the body, dropped a fence, kept the anchor lines, or stripped body lines that look like options would fail. I found no gap.
